🚀 Complete Deployment Guide: Database, Backend & Frontend
This guide details how to deploy your Student Attendance Management System to production cloud platforms.

🛠 Project Architecture Summary
Database: MySQL (Hosted on Railway or Aiven)
Backend: Java Spring Boot (Hosted on Railway or Render)
Frontend: React + Vite (Hosted on Vercel)
Part 1: Deploying the Database (MySQL)
Option A: Using Railway MySQL (Recommended)
Log in to Railway.app.
Click "+ New" → "Database" → Select "MySQL".
Railway will provision a managed MySQL database and display connection credentials under the "Connect" / "Variables" tab:
MYSQLHOST
MYSQLPORT
MYSQLDATABASE
MYSQLUSER
MYSQLPASSWORD
Note down these connection values or use Railway's internal variable references.
Option B: Using Aiven MySQL Cloud
Create a free account on Aiven.io.
Create a new MySQL service.
Obtain your Service URI: jdbc:mysql://<HOST>:<PORT>/<DATABASE>?useSSL=true&serverTimezone=UTC
Obtain the username (avnadmin) and password provided in the console.
Part 2: Deploying the Backend (Spring Boot)
Your backend has a production-ready 
dockerfile
 in the backend/ directory.

Step 1: Deploy to Railway
Push your project repository to GitHub.
In Railway, click "+ New" → "GitHub Repo" → Select your repository.
Set the Root Directory to /backend.
Railway will automatically detect the dockerfile and build your Spring Boot JAR.
Step 2: Configure Backend Environment Variables
In Railway → Go to your Backend Service → Settings / Variables tab, and add:

Environment Variable	Value Example / Description
DATABASE_URL	jdbc:mysql://${{MySQL.MYSQLHOST}}:${{MySQL.MYSQLPORT}}/${{MySQL.MYSQLDATABASE}}?useSSL=false&serverTimezone=UTC&allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true
DATABASE_USERNAME	${{MySQL.MYSQLUSER}} (or your db user)
DATABASE_PASSWORD	${{MySQL.MYSQLPASSWORD}} (or your db password)
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS	https://your-frontend-app.vercel.app
MAIL_USERNAME	shaikirshan78@gmail.com
MAIL_PASSWORD	your-app-password
Once set, Railway will assign a public domain URL to your backend (e.g., https://your-backend.up.railway.app).
Part 3: Deploying the Frontend (React + Vite)
Step 1: Deploy to Vercel
Log in to Vercel.com.
Click "Add New..." → "Project" → Import your GitHub repository.
Set the configuration as follows:
Framework Preset: Vite
Root Directory: frontend
Build Command: npm run build
Output Directory: dist
Step 2: Configure Frontend Environment Variables
Before clicking Deploy, add the environment variable:

Environment Variable	Value
VITE_API_BASE_URL	https://your-backend.up.railway.app/api
(Replace your-backend.up.railway.app with your actual Railway backend URL).

Click Deploy. Vercel will give you a domain (e.g., https://your-frontend-app.vercel.app).
Part 4: Final Linkage & Verification
Copy your Live Vercel Frontend URL (e.g., https://your-frontend-app.vercel.app).
Go back to Railway → Backend Service → Variables.
Update CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to include your live Vercel URL:
env

CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-frontend-app.vercel.app
Test your deployment:
Open your Vercel URL in your browser.
Test Sign In & Registration.
Verify that requests successfully talk to your Railway backend and read/write to MySQL.
